title: 2026-10-22_VoIP_Platform_Compromise_Investigation_335
description: Investigate and respond to a Linux/CDRThief malware compromise on a VoIP platform infrastructure.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The organization has detected unusual network activity on its VoIP platform infrastructure. As an incident responder, your task is to investigate the compromised systems, identify the malware, and contain the threat.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: You have SSH access to the target VoIP platform server (target) with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. From this server, you can investigate the compromise and access other connected systems as needed. Enter `start` to begin the investigation.
levels.local_content: You have SSH access to the target VoIP platform server (target) with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. From this server, you can investigate the compromise and access other connected systems as needed. Enter `start` to begin the investigation.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content: Identify and investigate an unauthorized or suspicious service running on the target VoIP platform server. Enumerate running services and distinguish legitimate from suspicious services.
levels.solution: Check running services and look for any that seem out of place or unrelated to VoIP operations. The suspicious service is likely related to the Linux/CDRThief malware. The final flag is `bkd.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check running services and look for any that seem out of place or unrelated to VoIP operations.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services that are not part of the standard VoIP platform configuration.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl status` followed by the service name to check its status and details.

levels.title: Determine Persistence Mechanism
levels.content: Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot. Identify persistence mechanisms (e.g., systemd, cron, scheduled task).
levels.solution: Investigate system startup configurations and look for entries related to the suspicious service. The persistence mechanism is likely a systemd service. The final flag is `payload-transfer.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Investigate system startup configurations and look for entries related to the suspicious service.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Check systemd service files and cron jobs for any suspicious entries.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl cat` followed by the service name to view its configuration file.

levels.title: Locate Malicious Artifact
levels.content: Locate the executable or file associated with the suspicious activity. Correlate processes with files on disk and identify malicious artifacts.
levels.solution: Search for files related to the suspicious service and check their properties and contents. The malicious artifact is likely a file with a suspicious name or path. The final flag is `/usr/local/bin/payload-transfer.sh`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Search for files related to the suspicious service and check their properties and contents.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for files with suspicious names or paths that are not part of the standard VoIP platform configuration.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use the command `ls -la` followed by the directory path to list files and their details.
